issues.verdictReason: start_setting_keyspace_for_connection (line 1330, marked `// TODO: There should be a timeout for this`, unchanged from main) still awaits connection.use_keyspace with no timeout. The PR moved the keyspace-mismatch check (connection_pool.rs:915-929) to run before maybe_reshard/shard_aware_port update instead of after, so a hung USE now also delays resharding and the shard-aware port update for that connection event, which previously happened immediately regardless of keyspace state.
issues.scopeReason: The missing timeout predates the PR, but the PR's reordering of the keyspace check ahead of resharding/port-update newly makes those updates wait on this hang-prone future.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: The keyspace-setup future still has no timeout, so a USE request that hangs keeps the connection in ready_connections indefinitely. issues.title: Keyspace setup failure on an empty pool is reported as lost host connectivity
issues.verdictReason: The new `Err(ConnectionSetupError::Keyspace(err))` arm (lines 900-911) calls update_shared_conns(Some(err.into())) when the pool is empty, which sets MaybePoolConnections::Broken and, per emit_events (line 1158) and worker.rs:733 handle_connectivity_change_event, publishes ConnectivityChangeEvent::Lost -> HostEvent::Down to the configured HostListener, marking a TCP-reachable node as connectivity-lost purely because of a keyspace-level failure (e.g. bad/missing keyspace).
issues.scopeReason: This call path is new code added by commit 7f48315d.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: A keyspace failure on an empty pool goes through update_shared_conns(Some(err.into())). That moves the pool from Initializing or Ready to Broken and emits ConnectivityChangeEvent::Lost, so a keyspace-level error is reported as lost host connectivity.

reportedAsByRun.rafp-six-pass-batched-2026-10-08/quillst: A keyspace failure on an empty pool goes through update_shared_conns(Some(err.into())). That moves the pool from Initializing or Ready to Broken and emits ConnectivityChangeEvent::Lost, so a keyspace-level error is reported as lost host connectivity.

issues.title: Broken connection during USE is misclassified as a keyspace setup failure
issues.verdictReason: connection.use_keyspace propagates RequestAttemptError::BrokenConnectionError as UseKeyspaceError::RequestError(..); the new Keyspace-error arm (lines 900-911) treats this the same as a genuine keyspace problem - setting had_error_since_last_refill (increasing backoff) and, if the pool is empty, publishing ConnectionError::UseKeyspaceError - whereas cluster/worker.rs:783's use_keyspace_result treats RequestError(BrokenConnectionError) specially as a non-keyspace, connection-level condition.
issues.scopeReason: The Keyspace-error arm and its backoff/reporting behavior are new code from commit 7f48315d.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: A broken connection during USE (UseKeyspaceError::RequestError(BrokenConnectionError)) is now reported as a keyspace setup failure. It increases backoff and is published as ConnectionError::UseKeyspaceError instead of BrokenConnection. Sibling code in use_keyspace_result treats broken connections as non-keyspace errors.

reportedAsByRun.rafp-six-pass-batched-2026-10-08/quillst: A broken connection during USE (UseKeyspaceError::RequestError(BrokenConnectionError)) is now reported as a keyspace setup failure. It increases backoff and is published as ConnectionError::UseKeyspaceError instead of BrokenConnection. Sibling code in use_keyspace_result treats broken connections as non-keyspace errors.
